confirmed.verdict: Reproduced, but the gap is about half what was claimed. Home (ytd-rich-item-renderer --sift li.item): 3 runs per side gave +56 ms, then 5 runs gave +293 and +579 ms (original 2044/2367/2473 vs Sift 2100/2660/3052). Sift's Loading line shows at 0.86-1.3 s, before the original's first contentful paint. V8 trace of the first 2.3 s of the search load: Sift's content.js took 127 ms with Sift on and about 3 ms with it off (loadFont 26, openAtPost 9, run 8, dialogIn 7). Skip generic helpers such as dialogIn/findDialog, watchShadows, openAtPost and fillScreen, and wait cheaply for the first ytd-rich-item-renderer / ytd-video-renderer instead. Defer loadFont (two woff2 fetches plus FontFace.load) until after the first list draw or to requestIdleCallback. Re-measure with firstpaint.ts, 5 runs, on home and search. Build the round 12 base to settle the regression question.

confirmed.suspectedCause: doLines: when lineFits rejects a line for its language, keepTitle(m, DAY) is saved without retrying the next model in the chain, or the same model with a firmer language instruction.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced live and by mock. This is the same defect as the F1231 remainder, so track it once. Live: the current English home feed had no Persian titles, and 2 direct requests (4 Persian titles, lang en, gpt-6-luna) all came back in English. An English YouTube search with Persian results did reproduce it: results?search_query='بررسی آپدیت سامسونگ' (page lang en). Sift showed 9 of about 22 Persian rows with only the Persian title. After deleting their keep-title entries and capturing the worker's model calls (aicap.ts), the model answered in Persian for 8 entries. Most of them had long Persian description text in their context. Examples: 'بررسی تغییرات و قابلیت‌های جدید آپدیت One UI 9 سامسونگ' and '۱۰ ویژگی سامسونگ برای استفاده از قابلیت‌های گوشی'. No other model was asked for them. Sift then showed 'بررسی آپدیت جدید سامسونگ One UI 9' and 'بررسی آپدیت One UI 9 سامسونگ؛ …' with no English line. The cache held '\0keep-title' with exp = ts + 24 h. Mock: I replaced the worker's fetch so every model call answers in Persian, then sent one lang 'en' item. Result: one model call (openai/gpt-6-luna), reply {done:true} with no line, and keep-title cached for 24 h. In code (src/background/index.ts emit in doLines), done.add(id) runs before lineFits. On failure, keepTitle(m, DAY) runs, so the entry is never in r.left and never retried. Nothing is lost against the original, so medium at the low end. Side note, not claimed: one cached line was itself Persian ('تغییرات آپدیت Samsung One UI 6.0', about half Latin letters) and was shown on the English page, so lineFits let a mixed-script wrong-language line through.
confirmed.fix: src/background/index.ts doLines/ask emit: when lineFits fails on language, do not keepTitle at once. Collect the entry and re-ask once, either with the language spelled out (langName(want), e.g. 'English', and a note to ignore the context's language) or with the next model in the chain. Call keepTitle(m, DAY) only if that retry also fails. Optionally pass the language name, not just the 'en' code, in the per-item input and LINES_SYSTEM. Also tighten lineFits/scriptFits so a line whose non-Latin letters are in the title's script does not pass for 'en'.

confirmed.suspectedCause: figureImage keeps the slides that intersect the figure element's box and picks the first one. It still counts as framed (the figure's box is wider than .swipe, or the edge test includes it) and comes first in DOM order. confirmed.verdict: Confirmed, high. I reproduced it on 2 loads of the same 3-photo listing. After 'Image 3', Sift shows 00t0t (photo 1, alt '... Needs Repair 1'), and 'Image 3' has aria-pressed=true. The original's slides sit at 759 (00t0t), -441 (00N0N) and 159 (00c0c). With Sift switched off, elementFromPoint in the .swipe box returns 00c0c, and the original reads 'image 3 of 3' (shots: research/shots/skeptic-cl-sift.png and skeptic-cl-orig.png). Image 2 is correct. The cause is exact. figure.iw spans 159..761, but .swipe (overflow hidden) spans 159..759. Slide 1, at 759..1359, passes the framed test because 759 < fr.right - 1 = 760. It then ties slide 3 on width (600) and wins on DOM order, since the width loop only takes a wider image (w > bestW). main's figureImage (generic.ts:6329) is identical, so main has the bug too.
confirmed.fix: src/content/extract/generic.ts figureImage (about line 6333-6349). Rank framed images by how much of their area is visible inside the figure's box (or inside the nearest clipping ancestor with overflow hidden, here .swipe), not by width with DOM order breaking ties. Or count an image as framed only if at least half its width is inside the box. A 2 px sliver of the next slide must not win.

confirmed.suspectedCause: An inference from a focus trace and the code, not proven. The page's name.focus() during the replayed click fires sift-focus, which schedules followPageFocus with setTimeout(0). Later in the visit, the re-render for the page change has not run by then. So followPageFocus finds Sift's existing Rename <button> with the same data-ref, sees it already focused, and clears pageFocusTo. The next render turns that ref into a textarea. Preact reuses the old <button> node for the following control (Invite people), and focus stays on it. During boot the render runs first, so the follow finds the textarea. Lead: keep pageFocusTo for the next render when the matched control is not an editable field but the page element is now editable (contenteditable/input), or key controls by ref so a node is never reused for another control.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced on both fixtures, fx/r11int-focusclose.html and fx/r12int-focusportal.html, with my own script (scratchpad/skeptic-n0/rn.ts). Mouse click on Sift's 'Rename list: Groceries' 5 s after load, then typing ' and bread' and Tab: log ['editing','share open'], name 'Groceries', share box open. This failed in 3 of 3 runs on focusclose and 2 of 2 on focusportal. It also failed with a 3.5 s load wait. Keyboard (focus Rename, Enter, type XY, Tab) failed 2 of 2 on focusclose and 1 of 1 on focusportal. Sift's focus sits on 'Invite people', the log stays ['editing'], the name stays 'Groceries', and the page is left in editing. At 1.5 s and 2.5 s the text does reach the name. The original (Alt+Shift+S, click #name, same typing) gives ['editing','edit ended: Groceries and bread'] in 3 of 3 runs, so the difference comes from Sift, not the page. One part of the suspected cause is wrong. Preact does not reuse the node. My probe shows the focused Rename button [data-ref r8] is removed (isConnected false). Sift renders a textarea [data-ref r8] for the name. Focus then lands on a different node, the 'Invite people' button [ra]. Sift's window-capture focusin listener swallows that focusin. The move comes from paint() calling refocus(). twinOf() wants the same tag, so the textarea with the same ref does not count. The first 'near' control wins, which is 'Invite people'. The rest of the suspected cause matches the code. The setTimeout(0) followPageFocus already ran against the old Rename button. That button was focused, so it cleared pageFocusTo, and the followPageFocus() call after paint does nothing. In the early runs the trace shows the same jump to 'Invite people', and then followPageFocus moves focus on to the textarea. Unclaimed side note: even when it works (1.5 s, 2.5 s), the typed text lands at the start ('edit ended:  and breadGroceries'). The original gives 'Groceries and bread'.
confirmed.fix: src/content/index.ts twinOf() (~311): when spot.ref is set, accept the control with the same data-ref even if its tag changed, at least a button that became an input or textarea. Then refocus keeps focus on the same page element instead of falling through to spot.near. Also, followPageFocus() (~3396) should not clear pageFocusTo when the matched ctl is not an editable field but to.el now is (isContentEditable or input/textarea). Keep it for the call after paint(). When following into a textarea that stands for a contenteditable, put the caret where the page's selection is, or at the end, so typing appends as on the original.
